extracted.intended_audience: general English readers interested in military history / contemporary newspaper readers
extracted.subtask_description: Advice and implicit standards for composing a personal, eyewitness narrative of a military campaign—balancing historical record, personal recollection, descriptive scenery, and operational detail for a general readership.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explain author's personal connection
rubrics_metrics.description: "It will be sufficient if, in the interests of coherency, I explain my connection with the Malakand Field Force."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State your relationship to the events (e.g., press correspondent, attached officer) so readers understand perspective and credibility; keep the explanation brief and relevant to coherency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Weigh eyewitness detail against justness of proportion
rubrics_metrics.description: "It may be doubtful whether an historical record gains or loses value when described by an eye-witness...what the narrative gains in accuracy of detail, it may lose in justness of proportion."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware that first-hand accounts can provide accurate detail but may overemphasize incidents that affected the narrator; balance vivid particulars with broader perspective to avoid distortion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adopt a personal narrative style when it increases interest
rubrics_metrics.description: Original aim was to present a picture of the war to Englishmen at home; the author is "inclined to think, that this end will be more easily attained by the adoption of a style of personal narrative."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use personal narrative to make the account more graphic and vivid; accept a loss of 'dignity of history' only when each step toward informality brings a corresponding increase in reader interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include local/specialised facts to form a true impression
rubrics_metrics.description: "Many facts, too local, too specialised, too insignificant, for an historical record, and yet which may help the reader to form a true impression of the scene and situation, are thus brought within the compass of these pages."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Don't omit small, local details simply because they seem insignificant historically—such specifics help readers imagine the scene and understand conditions on the ground.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid boring the reader with excessive personal matters
rubrics_metrics.description: "I do not desire to bore the reader or depreciate the story by the introduction of personal matters."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include personal anecdotes selectively; ensure they serve the narrative or illuminate the subject rather than divert or diminish the main account.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record troop movements clearly and concisely; make them skippable
rubrics_metrics.description: "To record the actual movements of troops in a campaign, is among the most important duties...For the sake of clearness, of brevity, and that the reader who is not interested may find convenience in skipping, I shall at once describe the whole of the marches and manoeuvres."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Present operational details (marches, manoeuvres) in a clear, concise section; signal or structure them so uninterested readers can skip while specialists can find the information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide orders of battle and precise casualty/composition figures
rubrics_metrics.description: The text lists unit compositions (brigades, regiments, batteries) and casualty totals, e.g., "a total of about 750 men... The casualties were as follows... Total Casualties, all ranks—72."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When relevant, give concrete lists of units involved, transport/armament, and accurate casualty figures—these details are central to a campaign account's factual utility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimise use of purely local terms and native names; explain terms when used
rubrics_metrics.description: "The use of purely local terms in all writing is to be deprecated...I have zealously tried to avoid the ugly jargon of a degraded language...the term just employed has, however, been so freely used in the newspapers recently, that it is perhaps as well to explain its meaning. A Jirgah is a deputation of tribesmen."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid overloading the text with untranslated local vocabulary or many native names; if such terms are used, define them plainly for the target readership to prevent confusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Convey routine background without excessive monotony
rubrics_metrics.description: "The narration of the daily movements of troops, unmarked by variety of incident, is dull and wearying...Yet he who would obtain a true idea of the soldier's life on service, must mentally share the fatigues of the march and the monotony of the camp."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include background routine and hardships to give readers a realistic sense of service life, but render these elements economically and with occasional illustrative detail to avoid tedium.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use signposting to separate scenic digressions from operational narrative
rubrics_metrics.description: "...after the Malakand Field Force is safely camped at Ghosam, the reader will be invited to return to examine the scenery, and remark the incidents of the way."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Structure the narrative so operational/chronological content and scenic or anecdotal digressions are clearly signposted or compartmentalised, enabling varied reader interest to be accommodated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Employ vivid descriptive language and evocative comparisons
rubrics_metrics.description: Passages use evocative imagery and historical allusion (e.g., relics of Buddhists leading mind back to earlier times; comparisons to amphitheatre scenes) to enrich description.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use figurative language and concrete imagery to make scenery and historical reflection compelling for general readers, while avoiding overwrought ornament that obscures facts.
